mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a quarter indicates a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a downturn in economic activity and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over 3 months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically boosts economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST increases by more than 5% in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a quarter signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face reduced output and profitability.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 2% in a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure during a tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is above 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month, combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2%, signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a quarter signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically boosts economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where RSAFS increases by more than 1% in a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) is below its 12-month moving average and GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative, it indicates a supply-side recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average and GDPC1 growth is negative.
